newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends lower in Europe on trade, rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends lower in Europe on trade, rate concerns.

text.p: The dollar ended 1-1/2 yen lower in Europe on Monday to its lowest level in four weeks, weighed down by concerns about Japan's rising trade surplus and receding hopes of a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates, analysts said.

The dollar also retreated by more than pfennig against the mark. A combination of sterling sales, after soft UK output data for May, and some additional jitters about a delay to European monetary union helped support the German currency, traders said.
"Yen strength started the move and we feel the dollar/yen pullback has further to go," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Japan's trade surplus for the first 20 days of June rose 129 percent from the same period last year to 453 billion yen.
"The rising Japanese trade surplus will be a fact of life for the market for months," said Meggyesi at DMG, who sees the dollar testing this year's low about 110.50 yen again soon.
Meggyesi said the yen rise has persisted despite a softening of Japanese interest rate rise expectations.

One factor buoying the yen may well be large scale dollar sales by south east Asian central banks, who are preparing to defend their currencies from any regional contagion from the recent currency crisis in Thailand, he said.
At 1525 GMT, the dollar was trading at 112.25/35 yen compared with 113.77/87 late on Friday and just off a four-week low at 111.98 set in early trade.
Against the mark, it was at 1.7455/60 compared with 1.7574/79 late last week.
The dollar displayed a generally softer tone on Monday following last Thursday's U.S. employment report for June.

Although the headline rise in non-farm payrolls was broadly in line with expectations, the unemployment rate rose to 5.0 pct from 4.8 percent in May and average earnings growth remained modest at just 0.3 percent. Rate rise talk was dampened further.

The more benign outlook for U.S. interest rates was supported by an article on Monday in U.S. magazine Business Week. The story cited a Federal Reserve source saying Fed chairman Alan Greenspan appears more tolerant of faster growth and lower unemployment than in the past.
The easier dollar in Europe was reinforced in early trading by continuing disquiet in German political circles about a timely start to EMU without strict economic targets being met.
Bavarian prime minister Edmund Stoiber argued in Monday's Financial Times for a "controlled delay" to the start of the single currency project if the risk was one of a weak euro.
Dealers said the reaction was limited, however, as Stoiber has held this view for some time and is still a minority view in the existing German government.

"We'd have to see that sort of comment come from someone like (German finance minister Theo) Waigel or (German Chancellor Helmut) Kohl before there would be a blowout of the prevailing market opinion," said a foreign exchange salesman at a French bank in London.
Dollar/mark was also weighed down by sterling/mark sales. however, as a wave of profit-taking set in on the pound's stellar rise to near six-year highs last week.

Sterling fell more than two pfennigs after news of an unexpected 1.1 percent drop in UK manufacturing output in May, which threw some cold water on talk of a UK interest rate rise of up to half a percentage point on Thursday.
Analysts said a quarter-point rate rise was still likely, however, after last week's government budget plan for 1997/98 did not clamp down hard enough on rampant consumer demand.
Elsewhere, the Mexican peso firmed a touch after weekend elections showed the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party lost its congressional majority for the firt time in 68 years.
--Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6762
